title: Incident compact rail: anchored quick-links, SLO scaffold, and postmortem anchors
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Design a compact, persistent 'incident rail' — a right-anchored collapsible strip that stays visible while users browse the incident timeline and alert details. The rail surfaces: concise alert rule metadata, SLO delta mini-sparklines, one-click on-call transfer + contact card, and direct anchors to the postmortem doc and related dashboards. Goal is to reduce context switching during triage and speed postmortem creation while preserving a low visual footprint for high-volume incident lists.
comments: 2025-03-13 - Maya Chen: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Two variants: 'compact pill' (collapsed) and 'expanded rail' (timeline-aware). Shared with PM/Eng for early feedback.
2025-03-14 - Priya Singh (ENG): Likes SLO sparkline idea; flagged backend work to provide per-incident SLO delta metrics (ENG-112882). Asked for API contract sketch.
2025-03-16 - Jonah Patel (PM): Emphasized single-click postmortem anchor must prefill incident metadata. Requested that cost delta (approx token cost) be optional behind a flag to avoid noise.
2025-03-18 - Accessibility review by Nora Alvarado (Design): Keyboard focus, ARIA labels, and high-contrast color tokens added to design. Suggested testing with screen readers on collapsed variant.
2025-03-19 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Prototype handoff to Eng scheduled; created spike ticket to validate layout across breakpoints. Noted two micro-interaction questions for design review meeting.

acceptance_criteria: Persistent rail appears on incident detail and timeline views and can be collapsed to a pill while preserving keyboard accessibility.
Rail shows alert rule name, severity badge, last evaluation timestamp, and link to alert rule editor.
SLO section displays current SLO value, delta vs. baseline, and a 3-point sparkline; clicking opens SLO detail pane.
One-click on-call transfer opens a minimal modal with suggested responders and 'notify' options; contact card links to user profile.
Postmortem quicklink opens a new draft in the postmortem editor with incident metadata prefilled (title, start/end times, primary contacts, related alerts).
Optional cost delta toggle displays an estimated token/cost delta for the incident when enabled by org settings.
Component passes accessibility checklist: tab order, ARIA labels for each interactive region, and screen reader announcement on expand/collapse.
Engineering integration verified: required APIs documented and spike completed (see dependencies).
design_decisions: Keep the rail right-anchored to align with typical incident timeline overflow and avoid occluding primary content.
Use a collapsed 'pill' that expands on hover/focus or explicit click to minimize visual clutter for responders scanning multiple incidents.
Surface minimal SLO context (value + delta + sparkline) rather than full graphs to reduce cognitive load; link to deep SLO view for analysis.
Make postmortem quicklink prefill limited to non-sensitive metadata; explicit confirmation required before creating documents to avoid accidental disclosures.
Expose cost-delta as an org-level toggle: default off to prevent noise for teams that don't track token economics during on-call.
Design for 3 states: hidden (mobile narrow widths), collapsed pill, expanded rail. Mobile behavior collapses to a bottom sheet pattern if needed.
usability_findings: Unmoderated tests (n=8) with SREs: average time to open postmortem editor reduced from 43s to 12s when using quicklink.
During prototype testing participants mis-clicked the contact card area when the pill was too small; increased hit target to 44px mitigates this.
Some users expected the SLO sparkline to be interactive; clarified affordance by adding a dedicated 'open SLO' chevron and hover tooltip.
High-frequency responders asked for a 'pin' option to keep the rail expanded for the session; added as a low-friction toggle on the rail header.
